summary:
Addressed every reviewer finding from reviewer-2026-09-20T015000Z. CRITICAL: added the `@username` sub-line to all 4 PendingChallenges rows (web received+sent, mobile received+sent), placed between the name line and the timeLeft countdown so identity reads as one block and the countdown keeps its own line — a username-only stranger's handle is now on screen in both trees. Landed a 4-case mobile render test (tests/components/mobilePendingChallengesIdentity.test.tsx) that mounts the real PendingChallengesSection through the @app alias, asserts against real climberHandle() output (never a hardcoded pseudonym), and covers received, sent, no-username, and display-name-set rows; proved it fails (2/4 red, 'expected [...] to include @bobsmith') with the sub-line removed. WARNINGS: (1) challenge accept + decline notification bodies now use climberDisplay(recipient.id, recipient.display_name) — the whole challenge flow (received/accepted/declined) names the same person identically; `rg '?? username|"Your opponent"' app/api` leaves only duel/[id]/rematch/route.ts:73, which is the duel flow the reviewer scoped to a follow-up ticket and has no `?? username` chain. (2) Added "@app/*": ["./src/*"] to app/tsconfig.json paths; proved the gap was real by removing it again — `pnpm typecheck` goes red with TS2307 on both PendingChallengesSection.tsx and the new test. Side benefit: the mobile challenge component is now inside the root TS program, so CI's `pnpm typecheck` typechecks it for the first time. (3) Extracted the search gate once into app/src/lib/userSearchQuery.ts (EMAIL_SHAPE, UserSearchFilter, exactMatchFilter, isSearchableQuery, searchFailureMessage) and wired all three call sites to it — route via relative import, web via ../../lib/userSearchQuery, mobile via @app/lib/userSearchQuery; pure extraction, isSearchableQuery is exactMatchFilter(q) !== null which is behaviourally identical since `valid` implies `username`. Deliberately structural (no Prisma import) so the mobile bundle never pulls in ORM types. (4) Both search components now have the missing !res.ok branch: clear results (so the previous query's Add/Challenge row can never sit next to a different query), set a user-visible error (429 distinguished), reuse notifyError() on mobile as the existing Add-failure path does, and clear the error on the next keystroke; the catch path uses the same shared copy. MINOR: FriendsList showUsername -> Boolean(...); the fragile `not.toContain("@")` now asserts on the row's

lines (no line starts with '@'); DuelHome drops the duplicated placeholder prop and inherits UserSearch's default. Gates: pnpm lint clean, pnpm typecheck clean, `npx tsc --noEmit -p mobile/tsconfig.json` unchanged at the same 4 pre-existing errors (GuestShell/ClimbScreen/ProfileScreen — verified identical on a stashed tree), pnpm test 82 files / 752 passed (baseline 748 + 4 new) in 8.2s, node scripts/hygiene.mjs clean. Committed on claude/lucid-fermat-3cbvbc, not pushed.
goal: Fix the reviewer's critical PendingChallenges information-loss finding plus all 4 warnings and 3 minors, without touching the explicitly out-of-scope duel-flow sites, blocked-friendship enforcement, or search-input a11y.

feedbackAddressed.finding: PendingChallenges / PendingChallengesSection have no @username sub-line, so the climberDisplay swap removed the only identifying information for a non-friend, display_name-null challenger.
feedbackAddressed.resolution:
Added `{c.sender.username && (

@{c.sender.username}

)}` to both received blocks and `{c.recipient.username && …}` to both sent blocks, inside the existing min-w-0 column, above the timeLeft countdown (identity lines together; countdown keeps its mt-0.5 font-mono line). Classes copied from the FriendRequests / FriendRequestsSection sub-lines in the same tree, so the two surfaces stay visually identical. New test file mobilePendingChallengesIdentity.test.tsx covers the exact scenario (sender displayName:null username:'bobsmith') and was proven red before the fix.

feedbackAddressed.finding: challenge accept/decline notification text still used display_name ?? username ?? "Your opponent".
feedbackAddressed.resolution: accept/route.ts: climberDisplay(c.recipient.id, c.recipient.display_name) (result.challenge is ChallengeWithUsers, recipient.id present). decline/route.ts: climberDisplay(challengeBefore.recipient.id, challengeBefore.recipient.display_name) — the decliner IS the recipient. `data.recipientName` shape unchanged. Swept by pattern, not literal: `rg '?? username|"Your opponent"' app/api` now matches only duel/[id]/rematch/route.ts:73 (duel flow, reviewer-scoped follow-up; it names a duel player, not a challenge party).

feedbackAddressed.finding: app/tsconfig.json lacks @app/*, so any file pulling a touched mobile component into the root program fails typecheck, and the new vitest alias had zero consumers.
feedbackAddressed.resolution: Added "@app/*": ["./src/*"] next to "@/*" (no baseUrl change, exclude untouched). The new mobile render test imports climberHandle from "@app/lib/handle" AND the component by relative path, so the alias has two consumers and the mobile component is now in the root program. Proven load-bearing: deleting the paths entry again makes `pnpm typecheck` fail with TS2307 at PendingChallengesSection.tsx:3 and the test file.

New app/src/lib/userSearchQuery.ts owns EMAIL_SHAPE, UserSearchFilter, exactMatchFilter, isSearchableQuery and searchFailureMessage. Route imports exactMatchFilter; web UserSearch and mobile UserSearchSection import isSearchableQuery + searchFailureMessage. No local copies remain (`rg 'EMAIL_SHAPE|isSearchable|exactMatchFilter'` shows only the lib and its importers). Behaviour identical; the existing usersSearch.route.test.ts now exercises the client gate transitively.

feedbackAddressed.finding: Both search components ignored non-ok responses, leaving a stale result row (with its Add button) next to a different query.
feedbackAddressed.resolution: Added the else branch in both: setResults([]) + setSearchError(searchFailureMessage(res.status)); the catch does the same with searchFailureMessage(null). Mobile also fires notifyError() (the existing Add-failure pattern). The query effect clears searchError on every keystroke, and the 'No user found' line is now gated on !searchError so the two never stack. 429 gets its own copy. The auto-fire prefix behaviour was left as-is (reviewer's suggestion (a) was 'consider', and changing it would alter the shipped gate).

feedbackAddressed.finding: FriendsList used `username !== null` where five siblings use truthiness.

feedbackAddressed.resolution:
Now collects the row's

textContents and asserts `lines.filter(t => t.startsWith("@"))` is empty, plus the positive name line — immune to Tailwind @-variants, mailto links and data URIs.

feedbackAddressed.finding: DuelHome duplicates UserSearch's default placeholder string.
feedbackAddressed.resolution: Dropped the `placeholder` prop at that call site; the prop remains available for other callers. One copy of the string.

learnings.insight: When a row's secondary slot is already occupied (PendingChallenges' second line is the expiry countdown), adding the identity sub-line means the row becomes three lines, not two. Putting `@username` directly under the name and leaving `timeLeft()` last keeps identity as one visual block and is the only ordering that matches the FriendRequests rows above it on the same screen — ordering matters here because both surfaces render the same flow and any drift is visible side by side.
learnings.action: Before adding a sub-line, read the row's existing second line. Insert the new line adjacent to the thing it identifies, not at the end of the column, and copy the class list from the sibling component in the same tree rather than inventing one.

learnings.insight: Adding "@app/*": ["./src/*"] to app/tsconfig.json does more than unblock tests: because tsc follows the import graph regardless of `exclude`, a single vitest test that imports a mobile/src component pulls that component (and everything it imports) into the root program, so CI's `pnpm typecheck` now typechecks mobile challenge components even though `exclude: ["mobile"]` stays and CI never runs `tsc -p mobile/tsconfig.json`. That is a real coverage gain, and also means a type error in a mobile component can now break the app typecheck gate.
learnings.action: Treat one render test per mobile component as the cheapest way to get that component into the root typecheck program. Conversely, when a mobile-only type error appears in `pnpm typecheck`, look for the test that dragged the file in rather than assuming the root include glob changed.

learnings.insight: Mobile (Capacitor SPA) components are testable in the existing vitest setup with no new dependencies and no module mocks beyond global fetch: @capacitor/core, @capacitor/haptics, react-router-dom and happy-dom all resolve from app/node_modules, Capacitor.isNativePlatform() returns false under happy-dom so the haptics helpers no-op, and wrapping the element in MemoryRouter satisfies useNavigate. apiFetch builds an absolute https://www.doomstack.lol URL, so a stubbed global fetch sees the real production code path.
learnings.action: Do not mock mobile/src/lib/api or lib/haptics to test a mobile component — stub global fetch and wrap in MemoryRouter. Assert on element textContent lists (container.querySelectorAll('p')) rather than innerHTML substrings so single-character negatives can't be satisfied by class names.

learnings.insight: The new production behaviour with no automated coverage is the search failure branch: on a non-ok response (429 in particular) both search components must clear `results`, keep `searched` false, and render the shared searchFailureMessage — the regression it prevents is clicking Add on the previous query's row. searchFailureMessage(status) is also a pure unit with three real callers and no test.
learnings.action: Add a UserSearch render case that resolves a 429 after a successful query and asserts the earlier result row (and its Add button) is gone and the 429 copy is present, plus a direct unit test of searchFailureMessage(429) / (500) / (null) and isSearchableQuery against the same fixtures usersSearch.route.test.ts already uses, so the client gate and the server gate are proven to be one function.

learnings.insight: Fix scope: 11 files modified, 2 added (1 lib, 1 test). Suite 748 -> 752 tests, 82 files, 8.2s (no runtime regression). Two gates proven to fail before being trusted: removing the mobile sub-line turns the new test red 2/4, and removing the tsconfig paths entry turns `pnpm typecheck` red with TS2307 x2. `tsc -p mobile/tsconfig.json` stays at the same 4 pre-existing errors (GuestShell TS6133, ClimbScreen TS2739, ProfileScreen TS2352) — unrelated to this diff and still unguarded by CI.
learnings.action: qa-acceptance: the manual pass the reviewer asked for still stands — an incoming challenge from a NON-friend with display_name null and a username set, on /duel and on the native Challenge screen; additionally verify the 429 search path shows the rate-limit copy with no stale result row. Orchestrator: consider adding `tsc -p mobile/tsconfig.json` to CI as its own step, or fixing those 4 errors, since the mobile project check is still not a merge gate.
